papers.title_in_file: Challenges and opportunities in the supervised learning of quantum circuit outputs
papers.what_it_is: A numerical study of whether neural networks trained by supervised learning can predict output expectation values of random CNOT and rotation circuits.

assertions.value: The authors report that the computational cost of supervised learning scales exponentially with the inter-layer variance of the random angles.
quotes: the computational cost of supervised learning scales exponentially with the inter-layer variance of the random angles.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from one study on one circuit family; no proof.

assertions.value: The authors report that, thanks to a scalable design, neural networks accurately predict the output of larger and deeper circuits than those used for training, including circuit sizes intractable for the most common simulation libraries.
quotes: neural networks accurately predict the output of larger and deeper circuits than those used for training, even reaching circuit sizes which turn out to be intractable for the most common simulation libraries
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result for circuits with only intra-layer angle variations.
assertions.reader_inference: The result applies to the restricted circuit family only, not to general circuits.

assertions.value: The authors state that further algorithmic or hardware developments, adopting some more specialized technique, might reach circuit sizes comparable to the one addressed in the article.
quotes: It is plausible that, in the near or midterm future, further algorithmic and/or hardware developments, in particular adopting some more specialized technique, might reach sizes comparable to the one addressed in this Article.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states the limit of its own intractability claim, Section 5, p.18.

papers.title_in_file: Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms in Open Quantum Systems
papers.what_it_is: Lecture notes covering the circuit model, variational algorithms, NISQ noise, error correction and error mitigation.

assertions.value: The author states that the notes are not intended to serve as a comprehensive review article.
quotes: The field is vast and the intent of these notes is not to serve as a comprehensive review article.
assertions.certainty_reason: The author's statement of the notes' scope, Preface p.i.

assertions.value: The notes describe the Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) as a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm that allows for optimising a cost function and finding an approximated solution.
quotes: The Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA) is a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm that allows for optimising a cost function and finding an approximated solution.
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition given in Section 2.5, p.20.

assertions.value: The author states that many quantum algorithms that come with guaranteed performance need millions of physical qubits, and that it could take decades to build fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of reaching this scale.
quotes: Many quantum algorithms that come with guaranteed performance need millions of physical qubits
It could take decades to build fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of reaching this scale.
assertions.certainty_reason: An unsourced statement of the field in lecture notes; a timescale is a forecast.
assertions.reader_inference: The decades figure is a forecast, not a measurement.

papers.title_in_file: A quantum advantage over classical for local max cut
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper comparing one-round QAOA with a one-round classical local algorithm on the LocalMaxCut problem for low-degree graphs.

assertions.value: The authors state that for the simplest degree-2 graphs the classical algorithm outperforms the QAOA on LocalMaxCut.
quotes: As these theorems show, for the simplest degree-2 graphs, the classical algorithm outperforms the QAOA.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1, p.2, with discussion on p.3.

assertions.value: The authors state that graphs with degree-3 allow for enough complexity that the QAOA outperforms the basic probabilistic classical algorithm.
quotes: In contrast, graphs with degree-3 allow for enough complexity that the QAOA outperforms the basic probabilistic classical algorithm.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 2, p.3 (degree-3 graphs with sufficiently large girth, in expectation).
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is against a one-round classical algorithm only, not against the best classical local algorithm.

assertions.value: The authors state that Hastings proves a classical local tensor algorithm outperforms the QAOA on MaxCut on triangle-free graphs, and that this work focuses on single round algorithms.
quotes: Hastings proves that a classical local tensor algorithm outperform the QAOA on MaxCut on triangle-free graphs.
Hastings local tensor algorithms are typically iterative but this work focuses on single round algorithms.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, Introduction p.2.

papers.title_in_file: The Spectral Geometry of Biregular Graphs: a Quantum Graph Approach
papers.what_it_is: A pure mathematics paper on the spectral theory of the Laplace operator on biregular quantum graphs (metric graphs).
papers.why_not: The paper is spectral graph theory on metric (quantum) graphs. It has no quantum computing or machine learning content; the word quantum names a graph model, not a computer.

papers.title_in_file: Warm-Starting QAOA with XY Mixers: A Novel Approach for Quantum-Enhanced Vehicle Routing Optimization
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of QAOA with a warm-start initialization and an XY mixer on 5-city Traveling Salesperson instances.

assertions.value: The authors report that the proposed combination of warm start and XY mixer consistently outperforms both baselines in terms of the percentage and rank of optimal solutions.
quotes: Results show that the proposed combination consistently outperforms both baselines in terms of the percentage and rank of optimal solutions
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study on small instances.

assertions.value: The authors state that simulations were performed on 5-city instances of the TSP, requiring 16 qubits, in a noise-free environment using the statevector method of Qiskit's AerSimulator and the COBYLA classical optimizer.
quotes: we conducted numerical simulations on 5-city instances of the TSP, requiring 16 qubits under the employed encoding scheme.
All simulations were performed in a noise-free environment using the statevector method of Qiskit's AerSimulator and the COBYLA classical optimizer.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section V.A, p.6.

assertions.value: The authors state that they tested 10 random instances of complete graphs, each with 5 different parameter initializations and circuit depths of up to 3 layers.
quotes: We tested 10 random instances of complete graphs, each with 5 different parameter initializations and circuit depths of up to 3 layers.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Section V.A, p.6.

papers.title_in_file: Generalized two-qubit Hamiltonian for Projective Quantum Feature Maps
papers.what_it_is: An experimental and simulation study of Hamiltonian-based projected quantum feature maps on four biomedical classification datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that the generalized two-qubit Hamiltonian family provides the most consistent pattern of statistically supported gains over matched classical baselines, although the performance of all methods depends on the dataset, encoding strategy, measured observables, and hardware conditions.
quotes: the generalized twoqubit Hamiltonian family provides the most consistent pattern of statistically supported gains over matched classical baselines, although the performance of all methods depends on the dataset, encoding strategy, measured observables, and hardware conditions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on four datasets.

assertions.value: The authors state that, taken together, their results do not yet establish quantum advantage.
quotes: Taken together, these results do not yet establish quantum advantage, but they provide empirical evidence that projected quantum feature maps can generate
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit in the Conclusion, Section V, p.16.

assertions.value: The authors state that the experiments include executions on real IBM quantum processors with up to 156 qubits, as well as statevector simulations for complementary benchmarks.
quotes: The experiments include executions on real IBM quantum processors with up to 156 qubits, as well as statevector simulations for complementary benchmarks.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Introduction p.3.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum and classical processing with photonic quantum machine learning
papers.what_it_is: An experiment on a silicon photonic quantum reservoir processing device performing quantum state tomography and a classical task.

assertions.value: The authors report that the reservoir consistently provided higher accuracy of predictions than a photon-number-resolving benchmark, both in the QPU hardware implementation and in digital simulations performed using the Perceval Python package.
quotes: the reservoir consistently provided higher accuracy of predictions, both in the QPU hardware implementation and in digital simulations performed using the Perceval Python package
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one experiment on a small dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state that they experimentally implemented 100 quantum states prepared with random unitary matrices, and that 70 states were chosen at random as the training dataset with the remaining states used for testing.
quotes: In total, we experimentally implemented 100 quantum states, prepared by choosing random unitary Usource matrices.
From this dataset, 70 states were chosen at random to construct the training dataset, with the remaining states used for testing.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Results p.4.

assertions.value: The authors state that both the density matrix parameter space and the reservoir feature space scale exponentially with the number of modes or particles, and that this can result in an overwhelming workload for the classical network at the output, although the reservoir size scaling is mild as shown in Fig. 3.
quotes: scale exponentially with the number of modes or particles.
This results in a mild scaling of reservoir size as shown in Fig. 3 and discussed in the SI, but can result in an overwhelming workload for the classical network at the output.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit in the Discussion, pp.7-8.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Re-Uploading for Calorimetry: Optimized Architectures with Extended Expressivity
papers.version_note: The file is arXiv 2412.12397 v2 (31 Jan 2026), titled 'Quantum Re-Uploading for Calorimetry: Optimized Architectures with Extended Expressivity'. The record's id and path name the v1 title ('Optimizing Hyperparameters for Quantum Data Re-Uploaders in Calorimetric...'). Same arXiv paper, later version.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of a single-qubit quantum re-uploading unit on a three-class calorimetry classification task, with a small QPU run.

assertions.value: The authors report that, on a three-feature calorimetry classification task, single-qubit quantum re-uploading units obtain higher accuracy than the mono-encoded variational quantum circuit baseline at matched parameter count.
quotes: compare them, at matched parameter count, to a standard mono-encoded variational quantum circuit (VQC) baseline.
In this setting, QRUs obtain higher accuracy than the mono-encoded baseline.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one simulated task.

assertions.value: The authors report that an ablation indicates most gains occur at small depths, with diminishing returns as depth increases while training cost grows approximately linearly.
quotes: indicates that most gains occur at small depths, with diminishing returns as depth increases while training cost grows approximately linearly.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical ablation from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that key limitations include a small set of engineered features, a scalar-to-multiclass thresholding scheme, and a restricted baseline class focused on mono-encoding, and that the hardware run is not intended as a noise-robust performance benchmark.
quotes: Key limitations include the use of a small set of engineered features and a scalarto-multiclass thresholding scheme, as well as a restricted baseline class focused on mono-encoding.
This hardware run is not intended as a noise-robust performance benchmark
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state these limits in Section 5 (Conclusion).
